- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.7) and price is rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- When sentiment flips from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags; adjust forecast 1–3 days ahead to align with sentiment shift.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in early part of 30d window (e.g., days 1–10), it’s overconfident; reduce early forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- If true outcome shows sharp spike (e.g., >5% from prior day) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model often underreacts; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.5–1.0 oscillations, model tends to overfit short-term noise; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast.
- For long-term (15–30d) forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often underestimates mean reversion; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to align with historical mean.
